name: Deadwood Village
summary: In southern Felwood, Deadwood Village's furbolgs defend their rough wooden homes from all who approach. Once peaceful and close to nature, they fell to the demonic corruption that blighted the forest.

sections.title: A Fallen Tribe
sections.body:
Near Felwood's southern border, the Deadwood tribe gathers in its village. When demonic energies swept through the ancient woodlands, the furbolgs could not resist the creeping rot. Fel malice warped their minds, and they abandoned their traditions and harmony with nature.

Now brutes, shamans, and den watchers defend their polluted grounds against intruders. Their violence brings despair to their uncorrupted cousins, the Timbermaw.

faq.q: Why are the furbolgs here hostile?
faq.answer: Demonic corruption overcame the furbolgs of Deadwood Village when Felwood was blighted during the Third War. Fel magic twisted their natural instincts into rabid aggression, leaving them violently insane and hostile to outsiders.

faq.q: Can players talk to or make peace with Deadwood Village?
aliases: can you be friendly with deadwood
faq.answer: No. The Deadwood tribe is too deeply corrupted for peace. Adventurers hunt them for tribal feathers and to win favor with the uncorrupted Timbermaw furbolgs, who guard the tunnels to the north.

faq.q: How does this tribe relate to the Timbermaw?
faq.answer: The Deadwood and Timbermaw were once furbolg tribes that lived in harmony with nature. When Felwood was corrupted, the Timbermaw kept their sanity, but the Deadwood fell to fel madness. The Timbermaw now see them as fallen and dangerous.

angles.text: As a druid, Deadwood Village shows how deeply demonic corruption can twist peaceful creatures and how nature's defenses can fail.
